items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: "Same way with Benny Goodman. I don't remember now what his first big hit was."

ctx.x: He had a lot of the musicians that he'd known. There aren't so many of them left. He didn't have Basie on for some reason, but some of his musicians. And a few of the blues things, unfortunately, they had his son on, too, who's a good guy, no doubt. But they had him on right after Sonny Terry, playing guitar and harmonica, which he should have. Actually, the young John Hammond likes Sonny Terry. He did a duet with him. As soon as it was over, he began applauding. I mean, he didn't try to steal the show. I mean,…

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-09-04
items.q: the first big popularity cycle of Benny Goodman had just made his big hit... Benny Goodman even that summer had become known as the world's greatest clarinetist.

ctx.x: I heard that song as a white religious piece.

Really? A religious group. The oldest record I ever came across was an old Paramount which wasn't anything very jazzy, you might say. a quartet. You know, a sacred quartet. But anyway, to get back to Dodds, I was surprised then, of course, that to me he was somebody famous. Anybody on the Louis Hot Five would be a famous musician. And he even had a sign out in the front. I was surprised that that was in the first big popularity cycle of Benny Goodman had just made his big hit out in California at the Palladium or…
